the 2019/2020 fires on the east coast were the most intense in recorded history and that the carbon emissions were unprecedented.
Australian forests are at risk of losing their capacity to store carbon as a result of climate change driven wildfires and that there are no simple answers for how to maximise carbon storage.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the impacts of climate change on forest ecosystems and how to mitigate the effects of climate change on forests and forest products.
the carbon cycle of forests in Australia, and in particular the role of wildfires.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the carbon stocks of Australian Eucalypt forest are declining, (2) the decline is driven by megafires and climate change, (3) prescribed burning is a poor tool to mitigate carbon loss, and (4) mechanical thinning of forests to reduce fire fuel loads also carries heavy carbon costs.
the 2019-2020 Australian wildfires were a major carbon source, and that the net impact on carbon storage in the future will depend on the future management of Australian forests.

the Australian forests have been severely affected by the megafires of 2019-20 and that the long-term consequences for the carbon stocks are unknown.
the carbon costs of fire management are significant.
the 2019/2020 Australian megafires were a disaster in many ways.

the loss of forest carbon is not a simple matter of counting the CO2 released during the fire.
the carbon stocks of Australia's forests are at risk from climate change.
